title: The Longest Free Time Between Two Meetings

concept.title: Merge the meetings, and the free times are the gaps between the merged blocks
body: An office has `n` meetings. Between meetings the room is free. What is the **longest stretch of free time that lies between two meetings** (not before the first or after the last)? For `(1, 3) (2, 6) (8, 10) (15, 18)` the meetings form the blocks `1-6`, `8-10`, `15-18`, so the free stretches are `6-8` (length 2) and `10-15` (length 5): the answer is 5. If all the meetings form one block, the answer is 0.

The meetings may overlap, so the free time is not simply "next start minus this end". Sort the meetings by the start and keep `cur_end`, the **latest end among all the meetings processed so far**. When the next meeting starts after `cur_end`, the time between them is free and has the length `start - cur_end`; remember the largest such gap. Then update `cur_end = max(cur_end, end)`.

body.code:
meetings.sort()
cur_end = meetings[0][1]
widest = 0
for start, end in meetings[1:]:
    if start > cur_end:
        widest = max(widest, start - cur_end)   # a free gap
    cur_end = max(cur_end, end)
print(widest)

body: The maximum ends so far is needed because a short meeting inside a long one must not shorten `cur_end`. Touching meetings (the next start equals `cur_end`) leave no gap. Sorting O(n log n) plus one scan O(n). This is the merging routine of the earlier problem, looking at the holes instead of the covered parts.

statement: `n` meetings are given; the meeting `i` takes the time from `start[i]` up to, but not including, `end[i]`. Between the earliest start and the latest end there may be moments with no meeting. Print the length of the longest stretch of time without any meeting that lies between two meetings, or 0 if there is no such stretch.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of meetings.
Each of the next `n` lines has two numbers `start` and `end`: the meeting takes the time from `start` up to (but not including) `end`.
outputFormat: Print the length of the longest free stretch.

examples.note: The free stretches are 6 to 8 and 10 to 15: the longest has the length 5.

hints: Sort the meetings by their start.
Keep the latest end of all the meetings seen so far.
A meeting that starts after that end leaves a gap of start - latest end.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
meetings = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: The meetings are sorted by their start; the latest end seen so far is kept, and every meeting that starts after it leaves a free gap of start - latest end. The largest gap is printed (0 if there is none).
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
meetings = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

meetings.sort()
cur_end = meetings[0][1]
widest = 0
for i in range(1, n):
    start, end = meetings[i]
    if start > cur_end and start - cur_end > widest:
        widest = start - cur_end
    if end > cur_end:
        cur_end = end
print(widest)
